enonce_intro_markdown: **(i)** In an experiment the length $l$ of a metal bar is measured many times and the observed values recorded. The recorded values are approximately normally distributed with mean 1.340 m and standard deviation 0.021 m. Find the probability that a recorded value
incertitudes: Question 5 (i) : les valeurs sont données avec la calculatrice (z exact $= 10/7 = 1.4286$) et la valeur de table (z arrondi à 1.43, $\Phi(1.43) = 0.9236$) est citée : (a) 0.0766 (table 0.0764) ; (b) 0.8469 (table 0.8472). Le résultat de (c), 1.313 m, est le même avec $z = -1.28$ (table) ou $z = -1.2816$.
Question 5 (ii) : l'heure d'arrivée (9:00 am) ne sert pas au calcul ; la densité exponentielle donne $P(T < 3) = 1 - e^{-9} = 0.999877$, arrondie à 0.9999.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $L$ be a recorded value: $L \sim N(\mu = 1.340,\ \sigma^2 = 0.021^2)$. Standardise with $Z = \dfrac{L - \mu}{\sigma} \sim N(0, 1)$:

$$z = \frac{1.37 - 1.340}{0.021} = \frac{0.030}{0.021} = 1.4286\ldots \approx 1.43.$$

$$P(L > 1.37) = P(Z > 1.43) = 1 - \Phi(1.43) = 1 - 0.9236 = 0.0764.$$

(With the exact $z = 1.4286$ a calculator gives $0.0766$.)

**$P(L > 1.37) \approx 0.077$** (0.0764 from the table, 0.0766 from a calculator).

The limits $1.31$ and $1.37$ lie $0.030$ below and above the mean $1.340$, so $z = \mp 1.4286$ and the required area is symmetric:

$$P(1.31 < L < 1.37) = P(-1.43 < Z < 1.43) = 2\Phi(1.43) - 1 = 2 \times 0.9236 - 1 = 0.8472.$$

(With the exact $z = 1.4286$: $1 - 2 \times 0.07656 = 0.8469$.)

**$P(1.31 < L < 1.37) \approx 0.847$** (0.8472 from the table, 0.8469 from a calculator).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that 10% of the recorded values are less than $l$,

(c) find, to three decimal places, the value of $l$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Here $l$ is the value such that $P(L < l) = 0.10$. Since $0.10 < 0.5$, the corresponding $z$ is negative. From the table of the normal distribution $\Phi(1.28) = 0.8997$ and $\Phi(1.29) = 0.9015$, so $\Phi(z_0) = 0.90$ gives $z_0 = 1.2816$ (more precisely) and by symmetry

$$P(Z < -1.2816) = 0.10.$$

$$\frac{l - 1.340}{0.021} = -1.2816 \;\Longrightarrow\; l = 1.340 - 1.2816 \times 0.021 = 1.340 - 0.02691 = 1.31309.$$

**$l \approx 1.313$ m.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** In a train station, the time $T$ in hours between the arrival of two trains is a random variable with an exponential distribution having the density function

$$f(t) = 3e^{-3t}, \quad t > 0.$$

A train arrived at 9:00 am. What is the probability that the next train will arrive in less than 3 hours.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$T$ has an exponential distribution with rate $\lambda = 3$ (mean waiting time $\frac{1}{3}$ hour). The next train arrives in less than 3 hours when $T < 3$:

$$P(T < 3) = \int_0^3 3e^{-3t}\,dt = \left[-e^{-3t}\right]_0^3 = 1 - e^{-9}.$$

$$e^{-9} = 1.234 \times 10^{-4} \;\Longrightarrow\; P(T < 3) = 0.999877\ldots$$

**$P(T < 3) = 1 - e^{-9} \approx 0.9999$**: it is almost certain that the next train arrives within 3 hours. The 9:00 am arrival time only fixes the origin of the waiting time.
